text.text_excerpt: Yelp 100? Done! The Joan of Arc Statue is my favorite New Orleans statue. I love that the statue sits in the middle of Decatur Street as if she is guarding the French Market from attack. I also love that unlike many other prominent statues, Joan is done in golden bronze and shines as if she were made of actual gold. There really isn't much more to say about this statue other than you should take a picture of it when you go to the French Market. Looking at the two previous reviews I notice that one review claims the statue has been in New Orleans since 1959 where the other says 1972. I wonder who is right. Update: After doing some of my own research I learned that the statue has been here ...

For my 100th Yelp review for the Yelp 100 challenge, I decided to review Joan of Arc. I absolutely love this statue. One of the many nods to France in our great city. She sits majestically on her horse on Decatur St.. She has become such a fixture in our city, that it's hard to believe she has only been here since 1959 when Charles de Gaulle came here and presented her to New Orleans on a state visit. I know it's probably a little hokey, but I like then there is a big Saints game and someone takes the liberty of attaching a Saints flag to her pole.

I'll keep this review short and not repeat the historical facts from other reviews. The Joan of Arc statue is a great landmark and a nice reminder of New Orleans's roots from France. Cast in bronze, the statue is kept polished and makes a great photo of any visit to the French Market.
